rationale: Use a broad scouting gradient to locate the elution window and critical pairs while minimizing the risk of missing strongly retained compounds. A midrange temperature leaves room to probe temperature-dependent selectivity in either direction.

Raise temperature while holding the gradient fixed to test selectivity around the sole critical pair. The current elution window leaves ample time margin, so prioritize improving that pair without sacrificing neighboring separations.
Test the upper temperature limit to map further selectivity changes in the central peak cluster. Monitor both the unresolved pair and the neighboring separation that narrowed at 50 C.

Use 55 C to balance the opposing temperature responses of the two central critical separations, and flatten the gradient to improve their resolution. The last peak should remain within the 10-minute scoring window given the current time margin.
The maximum CRF is secured, so shorten the gradient by one grid step to seek a faster fully resolved method. Check whether the marginal central pair retains R >= 1.5.

Slightly flatten the 12-minute gradient by lowering its endpoint one grid step. This should recover the small resolution deficit while eluting the last peak sooner than the fully resolved 14-minute method.

Shift both gradient endpoints upward while preserving the slope of injection 6 to seek earlier elution. This tests whether the faster starting conditions preserve the two marginal central separations.

With a maximum-score method secured, probe the low-temperature selectivity regime for an alternative route to faster full resolution. The broad gradient should still elute all compounds comfortably within the acquisition window.

Return to the favorable 55 C regime and lower the starting organic fraction to improve the central separation that deteriorated at higher phi0. The steeper slope than injection 6 may offset the added retention and yield a faster fully resolved method.

Lower the endpoint one step to recover the small resolution deficit in injection 9 while targeting a last peak earlier than 8 minutes. Monitor the other central pair closely because its R of 1.53 leaves little margin.

Test a higher-organic, high-temperature regime that may separate the central pair beyond its apparent elution-order crossover. This could substantially shorten elution, but requires checking both the central cluster and compression of the earliest peaks.

Lower the starting organic fraction to restore early-pair separation, while steepening the gradient to explore selectivity beyond the central crossover. This tests a substantially faster alternative to the fully resolved 55 C method.

Shorten the gradient another step to determine whether slope-driven selectivity can open the remaining central critical pair. Closely monitor its neighboring pair, which had only modest resolution margin in injection 12.

Test whether a higher starting organic fraction at 50 C can improve the unresolved central pair seen in injection 2 while preserving its neighboring separation. This explores a faster alternative without relying on the unfavorable 60 C crossover region.

Probe intermediate-low temperature with a modestly shallower gradient to seek a different fully resolved selectivity window. This may separate the central cluster before the crossings observed at higher temperatures, while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes.

Test whether a steeper gradient shifts the central selectivity enough to open the critical pair at 40 C. The maximum-score method remains secured; this injection explores a substantially shorter elution window.

Refine the successful 55 C region with a slope between injections 5 and 6, targeting full resolution with earlier elution than injection 6. This should slightly strengthen the pair that narrowly failed in injection 5 while preserving the other critical separation.

Preserve injection 10's successful gradient slope but end the programmed ramp two minutes sooner. Since its last peak eluted at 7.60 minutes, before this new gradient ends at the outlet, the separation should remain unchanged while shortening the programmed gradient.

Seek a more robust maximum-score method by combining the higher starting organic fraction with a shallower gradient. This should recover the central separation lost in injection 7 while retaining improved spacing of the other critical pair, with the last peak expected before 10 minutes.

Lower the endpoint one step to correct the small resolution deficit in injection 19. The other central pair has useful margin, and the last peak should remain below 10 minutes, potentially providing a more robust maximum-score alternative.

Increase the endpoint one step from injection 4 to test a faster gradient within the established fully resolved region. This should retain maximum CRF, with more resolution margin than the fastest successful method at phi0 0.05.

Preserve injection 6's fully resolving slope while shortening the programmed gradient to 8 minutes. Its last peak at 8.00 minutes precedes the new gradient endpoint at the outlet, so this method should retain the maximum CRF.

Shorten the successful gradient by another two minutes while preserving its slope through the central critical pairs. The final peak will encounter the hold and may elute later, so check whether full resolution and a last peak within 10 minutes are retained.

Refine the more robust fully resolved region near injection 20 with a slightly shallower slope and a shorter programmed gradient. This should improve its limiting separation while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes.

Slightly flatten injection 24's gradient to balance its two limiting separations and seek additional resolution margin while retaining CRF 1.000. The last peak is expected around 9.3 minutes, still before the time penalty begins.
